# What OpenRouter API keys the library redacts, and what it leaves alone.
#
# Every key here is built from the ordered run 0123456789abcdef, which no real
# credential is: the body is that run written four times, which is the
# sixty-four hexadecimal digits the pattern reads it at. The count is not an
# abbreviation — a body shortened for readability would leave a case holding no
# key at all — and its total with the prefix is the seventy-three characters the
# example in OpenRouter's own documentation is. Where the case is what a case is
# about the same run is written in uppercase, since the body is hexadecimal and
# holds the letters of either case.

patterns: openrouter-api-key

# A key as it is written. One string serves every model OpenRouter routes to,
# so what is below differs in where the key stands rather than in what kind it
# is: the response it is first read out of, which OpenRouter says is the only
# place a key is ever shown whole, and the bearer header it is sent in.

case: a key in an environment assignment
in:   OPENROUTER_API_KEY=sk-or-v1-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:  OPENROUTER_API_KEY=«openrouter-api-key»

case: a key in the response that first reports it
in:   {"key":"sk-or-v1-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef","data":{"label":"sk-or-v1-abc...123"}}
out:  {"key":"«openrouter-api-key»","data":{"label":"sk-or-v1-abc...123"}}

case: a key in a bearer token header
in:   Authorization: Bearer sk-or-v1-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:  Authorization: Bearer «openrouter-api-key»

case: a key on a command line
in:   curl -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-or-v1-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef" https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/key
out:  curl -H "Authorization: Bearer «openrouter-api-key»" https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/key

case: a key in a configuration environment block
in:   "env": {"OPENROUTER_API_KEY": "sk-or-v1-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef"}
out:  "env": {"OPENROUTER_API_KEY": "«openrouter-api-key»"}

case: a key at the end of a sentence
in:   the key is sk-or-v1-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef.
out:  the key is «openrouter-api-key».

# The alphabet. A body is hexadecimal, so the letters it may carry stop at f and
# neither the hyphen nor the underscore may stand inside one, however many
# hyphens the prefix is written with. Either case is read in the body, which the
# pattern's own file weighs: every key OpenRouter has printed is lowercase, and
# a scan asking for lowercase alone would locate nothing of a body the day
# OpenRouter wrote one in uppercase. The prefix is read in one case, and the
# case named "an uppercase prefix" below is what that comes to.

case: an uppercase body
in:   sk-or-v1-0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF
out:  «openrouter-api-key»

case: a letter past f at the end of the body
in:   sk-or-v1-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdeg
out:  sk-or-v1-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdeg

case: a hyphen inside the body
in:   sk-or-v1-0123456789abcdef-123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:  sk-or-v1-0123456789abcdef-123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef

case: an underscore inside the body
in:   sk-or-v1-0123456789abcdef_123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:  sk-or-v1-0123456789abcdef_123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef

# The length. Sixty-four is what OpenRouter's own example carries and what all
# three rulesets reading this format ask for, and it is read as a count and not
# as a floor, like the AWS access key ID, the GitLab token, the Google API key,
# the SendGrid key, the Sentry token, the Notion token, the Grafana token, the
# Supabase token and the RubyGems key, and unlike the OpenAI, Anthropic,
# Stripe, PyPI, npm and Linear bodies. What makes that wager small here is the
# version the prefix carries: a key of some other shape is a key behind some
# other prefix, so the count goes stale no sooner than sk-or-v1- does.

case: a body of sixty-four characters is a key
in:   sk-or-v1-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:  «openrouter-api-key»

case: a body one character short is not
in:   sk-or-v1-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcde
out:  sk-or-v1-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcde

case: a body run one character longer is a key and the character after it
in:   sk-or-v1-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0
out:  «openrouter-api-key»0

# What a key may be written against. There is no boundary on either side of the
# prefix — which is a disagreement with all three rulesets, since each of them
# writes one at both ends — so a key keeps its span whatever word character it
# abuts, and what stands past the seventy-third character stays where it was
# written. The first two cases are what a boundary in front would cost. The
# third is what it would buy, and it is all it would buy: the prefix closes with
# a hyphen rather than with a letter, so no snake_case name reaches it and only
# a hyphenated word spelled with these segments in this order does.

case: a key after an underscore
in:   OPENROUTER_API_KEY_sk-or-v1-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:  OPENROUTER_API_KEY_«openrouter-api-key»

case: a key after a letter
in:   xsk-or-v1-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:  x«openrouter-api-key»

case: a hyphenated word closing on the prefix
in:   risk-or-v1-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:  ri«openrouter-api-key»

case: a word written against a key
in:   sk-or-v1-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdefsuffix
out:  «openrouter-api-key»suffix

case: a hyphenated word written against a key
in:   sk-or-v1-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef-suffix
out:  «openrouter-api-key»-suffix

case: an underscored word written against a key
in:   sk-or-v1-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef_suffix
out:  «openrouter-api-key»_suffix

# Two keys written together. No key can be written inside another, which only
# the Stripe, Supabase and RubyGems patterns say beside this one: a candidate
# begins where an s begins, and the only s a span covers is the one its prefix
# opens with — the rest of the prefix is k, o, r, v, a digit and three hyphens,
# and a body is hexadecimal. So the spans here never overlap, and the scan may
# resume at the body of a candidate rather than a byte past its start. The
# second case is that resumption doing its work: the outer candidate is turned
# away at the first character of its body, which is the s the inner prefix
# opens with, and the inner key is found where it stands.

case: two keys with nothing between them
in:   sk-or-v1-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdefsk-or-v1-0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF
out:  «openrouter-api-key»«openrouter-api-key»

case: a candidate whose body opens with a prefix
in:   sk-or-v1-sk-or-v1-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:  sk-or-v1-«openrouter-api-key»

case: two keys separated by a space
in:   sk-or-v1-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef sk-or-v1-0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF
out:  «openrouter-api-key» «openrouter-api-key»

# A digest written behind the prefix, which every prefix in this package leaves
# as a collision and which this one pays rather than avoids. Sixty-four
# hexadecimal digits are a SHA-256, so the shape this pattern reads and the
# shape a digest is are the same shape — where the Grafana format has an
# underscore dividing its secret from its checksum to turn a digest away with,
# this one has nothing. Redacting it is right rather than a fault in it: a key
# OpenRouter issued is sixty-four hexadecimal digits behind this prefix, so a
# scan declining a digest behind this prefix declines every key there is. The
# shorter digests are turned away by the count, and a digest on its own carries
# no hyphen and so holds no prefix to be found at.

case: a sha256 behind the prefix
in:   sk-or-v1-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:  «openrouter-api-key»

case: a sha1 behind the prefix
in:   sk-or-v1-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567
out:  sk-or-v1-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567

case: an md5 behind the prefix
in:   sk-or-v1-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:  sk-or-v1-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef

case: a sha256 in a cache key
in:   key: 0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:  key: 0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef

# And what this pattern leaves alone. First the prefix: the case OpenRouter
# writes it in, the version written later, the version left out, and the hyphens
# written as underscores. Then a body of the right count with nothing in front
# of it, the prefix of an OpenAI project key in front of one, a key a space has
# broken, and the prose and the log line no pattern here has anything to find
# in.

case: an uppercase prefix
in:   SK-OR-V1-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:  SK-OR-V1-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef

case: a later version of the prefix
in:   sk-or-v2-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:  sk-or-v2-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef

case: the version left out of the prefix
in:   sk-or-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:  sk-or-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef

case: underscores where the prefix carries its hyphens
in:   sk_or_v1_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:  sk_or_v1_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef

case: a body of the right count opening with no prefix
in:   xx-xx-xx-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:  xx-xx-xx-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef

case: an openai prefix in front of a body of the right count
in:   sk-proj-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:  sk-proj-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef

case: a key broken by a space
in:   sk-or-v1-0123456789abcdef0123456789 abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:  sk-or-v1-0123456789abcdef0123456789 abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef

case: prose
in:   there is no credential in this sentence
out:  there is no credential in this sentence

case: a log line
in:   time=2026-08-17T00:00:00Z level=info msg="calling api" url=https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/chat/completions
out:  time=2026-08-17T00:00:00Z level=info msg="calling api" url=https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/chat/completions
